Ella has been waiting for some time. “Wait a sec, hon,” her Dad had said, patting her arm and leaning over to kiss her cheek. She's perfectly safe here; this is a good neighborhood and she can still see her Dad over by the 7-11, chatting to one of his old work buddies.

No, Ella's safe from absolutely everything except boredom, and as every kid knows, that's the real killer. She props herself up on the back seat and gazes through the dirty rear window, at the Christmas lights strung from the streetlamps, and the distant glowing smudge of the town Christmas tree. She squints her eyes half-closed, and imagines…

4323.d:
256 algorithmic drawings of the same flower

This system translates color into movement. A swarm of drawing particles, like virtual pencils, are guided by the color values of the pixels in an input image. The formulas performing the conversion put into play many parameters. The space of possibilities of the system is enormous, the variety of drawings endless. 256 is just a small arbitrary sample. 

This work can be seen as a playful reflection on the concept of “style”, which is so essential to our ideas about art and (human) artists. This short program can paint the same image on infinitely many “styles” – each of them reducible to a simple combination of mathematical parameters. 

The input image is a photo of a yellow hypericum flower I took during a holiday in the Argentinean Patagonia, near Bariloche, in 2016.

This is a new iteration of a generative exploration from 2016. You can see it at https://flickr.com/photos/solaas/albums/72157670059223206

Simulating an impressionist painting with a cubist layout. This is a long-running piece that can take up to 3 or more minutes to complete.

Press ’s’ to save a screenshot.
It will only draw if the browser window has focus, otherwise, it will pause.

Method:
- A quadtree is constructed from a variable distant poisson disc sample points on a noise field
- For each square in the quadtree ...
- Pick a random color or grey based on 3d noise (x, y, and time)
- New set of poisson disc sampled points are distributed based on 3d noise (x, y, and time)
- Points are used for brief particle simulation
- Path of those points are drawn with a brushstroke
- Once all of the squares are drawn, the time value increments and it loops back for another layer 10 times

Features:
- colorful: common, use full-color palette instead of colors and grey
- thick strokes: common, use thicker brush strokes
- smooth: common, smoother noise pattern
- particle can escape: rare, particles may extend beyond their bounding square

Created by Eko33, a generative artist featured at the Tezos Ecosystem Exhibition (Art Basel Miami 2021).

This generative artwork creates a limited series of distinctive artworks based on unique hash seeds.

The algorithmic approach of this collection generates a broad spectrum of unique outcomes, inspired by the "giant machine" from the movie "Modern Times."

Beyond a classic mechanical representation, Eko33 aims to convey multiple emotions while embracing the cold nature of algorithms.

Computer-generated generative art can be seen as a gigantic assembly line. Still, its true nature gives the artist complete freedom from all commercially available tools/constraints.

The collection "Modern Times" highlights the dark ages of generative arts using a bichromatic color palette and evolves toward the contemporary "Digital Renaissance" era using warmer, more acid and "pop" colors.

4397.d:
Mondrian artforms have specific traits when looked at through the perspective of generative art. They often have thick black stroke borders, use only primary colors, have similar number of white grids as it has the color grids, have a well-defined range of the grid sizes, et al.

This art changes this Mondrian idea. 

It uses light-weighted stroke only to provide some definition to consequent grids. 
It uses a mix of matte, semi-transparent and partly-greyish tones(to avoid primary colors and whites)
It also allows grids with a higher range. So you can have 50 large grids or even 2500 small ones. 

This artwork also stretches the entire window instead of a defined art-size as is the case with most Mondrian art.

Apophenia is the art of seeing things in patterns that aren't 'really' there.
Frogs and tadpoles, small waving aliens, turtles, seahorses and bits of elephant - our brains will search for something we recognise in the randomness and chaos.
This pattern is made by tessellating hexagons. There are 12 unique hexagon possibilities plus reflections and rotations which bring the total possible for each placement in the design to 46.
Features include a choice of 7 colour palettes, 11 scales and the drawing of a grid behind the main pattern or not. Most rare are the very large or small scale with grid lines in a colour that isn't Teal and Peach.

4457.d: "Electez" is a series of works that use digital cloud chambers to observe the traces of unidentified particles. When doing art creation, just like scientists discovering new particles, artists continue to draw interesting ideas from reality and fantasy to collide with each other, trying to find a unique existence at the moment of collision in the process of mixing ideas. The space in the work "Electez" is divided into parts with different physical characteristics, which affect the movement, rotation, splitting, and annihilation of particles. It is an unpredictable experimental system with unlimited possibilities to explore the intersection of physics, mathematics, and art.
